data.name: Dhruvatha
data.gender_notes: Dhruvatha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Dhruvatha is the name of a star that symbolizes unwavering faith and determination. The name Dhruvatha carries the meaning “Star of Dhruva” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhruvatha usually hope their child will grow to embody star of dhruva and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name representing divine guidance and constancy.
data.etymology: Dhruvatha belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Star of Dhruva.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhruvatha total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Dhruvatha" holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism. In ancient mythology, Dhruva is a prince who was cursed with exile due to a rash action. Even after being abandoned by his parents, Dhruva's unwavering devotion towards Lord Vishnu led him to attain a place in the heavens, symbolized by the star Dhruva or Polaris.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Dhruvatha" signifies steadfastness in one's spiritual journey and unyielding faith amidst life's challenges. The story of Dhruva serves as a inspiration for us to remain committed to our dharma - higher purpose or duty- despite the barriers we face in our path to self-realization and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dhruva, represented by the name Dhruvatha, embodies unwavering determination and devotion. Rooted like the pole star, he remains steadfast in his purpose amidst life's challenges, inspiring perseverance and faith.

vedic_reference.note: Mentioned in the Bhagavata Purana as the name of the Pole Star

historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, King Dhruva was a great devotee of Lord Vishnu. When he was only a child, he was cursed by his father, King Uttanapada. The curse forced Dhruva to wander in the forest in search of truth, penance and redemption. He vowed to meditate on Lord Vishnu until he was blessed with a boon. Lord Vishnu, moved by Dhruva's unwavering devotion, appeared before him and granted him the boon of eternal stability, which came to be known as the Pole Star, Dhruva Tara, or the North Star.

King Dhruva, also known as Dhruvadeva, was a ruler of the Ikshvaku dynasty. He ruled Ayodhya during the Treta Yuga, the second of the four yugas in Hinduism. Known for his unwavering devotion to Lord Vishnu, Dhruva was cursed by his father, King Prasenajit. The curse forced Dhruva to wander in the forest in search of truth and penance until he was blessed by Lord Vishnu, who appeared before him and granted him the boon of eternal stability, which came to be known as the Pole Star or Dhruva Tara.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern context, the ancient Hindu name 'Dhruvatha' is often used in various forms across different digital platforms. It is popularly seen in astrological contexts, where it refers to Dhruva, a celestial being and the pole star around which the North celestial pole revolves. This name is also used in spiritual and mythological contexts, where Dhruva is depicted as a virtuous prince who gained immortality and became the pole star. On Instagram and Twitter, users often post about the significance and spiritual meaning of the name Dhruva or share images and infographics related to astrology and mythology. On YouTube, there are numerous videos on the topic of Dhruva, including astrological predictions, spiritual teachings, and stories from Hindu mythology.
